item.title: Tailcat
item.description:
📝 The tailcat CLI (in cmd/tailcat) is built on the tailcat Go library (importable as github. Whether you use tailcat as a CLI tool or library, one side runs a tailcat server (listener) and gets back a short connection token. ) And then the client can: $ echo hello | tailcat tcomFwWCCcjS5nKNqAod034nWoJZW0LZqDhhC8U_dKdnDRYQ8uNGFpGQEu $ Then the server unblocks: $ tailcat # Selected bootstrap relay region 302, San Francisco # 🐈 Server listening with new address: tcomFwWCCcjS5nKNqAod034nWoJZW0LZqDhhC8U_dKdnDRYQ8uNGFpGQEu hello $ Expose local ports through the tunnel Or you can serve a local TCP port, forwarded to localhost: $ tailcat --serve=8080,8443 # or --serve=all # 🐈 Server listening with new address: tcXXXXXXXXX And then the client: $ tailcat tcXXXXXXXXX 8080 GET / HTTP/1.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/tailscale/tailcat

item.title: Designation of Autistici/Inventati as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist
item.description:
📝 Autistici/Inventati (A/I Collective) is an Italy-based extremist group that builds and operates the digital infrastructure for violent Antifa cells and other far-left militants across the world. A/I Collective’s Support for Violent Far-Left Extremist Groups The A/I Collective provides encrypted tools and services to numerous violent far-left extremist groups operating in the United States and around the world. The anarchist cells responsible for sabotaging rail systems across France, Italy, Germany, and the Netherlands in 2026, relied on A/I Collective tools and services to claim responsibility for the attacks, publish official communiqués, and disseminate manuals for constructing improvised incendiary devices to target railways and other critical infrastructure.
